ORDER This application, under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. (S.528 of BNSS) has been filed for quashment of FIR in Crime No.627/2023 registered for the offences under Sections 377, 498A, 323, 294 and 506, 34 of IPC and Sections 3, 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act as well as criminal proceedings of ST No.23/2024.
2.

Challenging the FIR as well as criminal proceedings, it is submitted by counsel for applicants that applicant No.1 is father-in-law, applicant No.2 is elder brother-in-law, applicant No.3 is wife of applicant No.2 and applicant No.4 is daughter of applicants No.2 and 3.
It appears that during the pendency of this application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., charges were framed against applicants No.1 to 3 and Vivek Singh.
Certified copy of the order framing charge has been filed in Criminal Revision No.4886/2024 and from the cause title it appears that only four accused persons are being prosecuted.
From the charge-sheet, it is clear that charge-sheet has been filed against applicant No.4 before the Juvenile Justice Board.
However, applicants have not prayed for quashment of criminal proceedings pending before the Juvenile Justice Board.
Instead of taking a hyper- NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19772 2 MCRC-6925-2024 technical view, this Court would consider the allegations made against all the four accused persons.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 has lodged an FIR on 15.07.2023 alleging that she was married to Vivek Singh on 25.02.2020.
Her parents had given cash amount of Rs.15,00,000/- as well as gold chain to other family members and three pairs of Tops and other household articles.
Her husband is in Indian Navy.
After marriage, she was never treated well by her in-laws.
Whenever her husband used to come on leave, then behaviour of her in-laws used to remain good, however, lateron they used to block her number and were not talking to her.
After one year of marriage, her mother-in-law/applicant No.3, her father-in-law/applicant No.2 and her husband Vivek Singh started maltreating her for demand of dowry.
Her sister-in- law also used to assault her and abuse her on daily basis.
However, in order to save her family life, she maintained silence and for fear of society neither lodged any report nor narrated the activities of her in-laws to her parents.

Later, her father- in-law/applicant No.2 and grand-father-in-law/applicant No.1 bought Rs.10,00,000/-, from her father by way of loan but whenever said amount was demanded back, then they used to threaten her and harass her physically and mentally.
Whenever her husband used to come back on leave, he also used to assault her.
Her husband had also blocked her mobile number and stopped talking to her.
In the month of August, 2022, when her husband came back home, then she enquired that how long such misbehaviour would continue.
Then she was assaulted by him.
Then the complainant informed her husband that if her in-laws will continue to misbehave with her and harass her, then she would be compelled to lodge a report and make a complaint to his unit.
It is also alleged that she had evidence that her husband had extra-marital ties.

Thereafter, her husband snatched her phone and left her to her parental home at Morena on the pretext that he would NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19772 3 MCRC-6925-2024 take her to Mumbai.
Thereafter, without any information to respondent No.2, a case for divorce was instituted.
When she received notice and called her husband then he did not talk to her.
When she talked to her in-laws then they took her to village but in the village also she was badly harassed by them.
In the month of February, 2023, she came to Morena to appear in examination and from the month of April she started residing in her matrimonial house.
On 19.06.2023, she went to the market to purchase certain notes.
Then applicant No.3/mother-in-law broke open the lock of the house and put a central lock and went to her parental home.
Therefore, she was compelled to stay outside of the house and no-one picked up her phone.
Thereafter, she talked to applicant No.2/father-in-law who suggested her to go to her parental home and accordingly, she went to her parental home.
On 26.06.2023, when she came back to her matrimonial house then she found that it was locked.
She made a complaint at Bahodapur Police Station and opened the house with the help of an additional key.

Thereafter on 27.07.2023, when her mother-in-law came back to her house, she started assaulting her and raised dispute with regard to opening of the house and also scolded as to how she had entered into the house.
When she narrated the entire incident to her parents then they convinced her not to lodge the report.
When her husband came back from leave then she was beaten by him.

On 14.07.2023 her husband directed that she would not be allowed to stay in the house and she was badly beaten by her mother- in-law/applicant No.3, sister-in-law/applicant No.4 and her husband Vivek Singh.
On 15.07.2023 also she was badly beaten by her mother-in-law, sister-in-law and her husband.
As a result, she sustained injuries on her hands, cheek and back and an attempt was also made to strangulate her.
Three days back, in spite of her resistance, her husband had committed unnatural sex with her.
Her mobile phone NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19772 4 MCRC-6925-2024 was also broken.
Somehow she entered the house of neighbour through roof in order to save her life and informed her parents on phone.
Accordingly, the FIR was lodged.

sentences.text: Challenging the FIR lodged by respondent No.2, it is submitted by counsel for the applicants that in fact the husband of respondent No.2 i.e. Vivek Singh had instituted a divorce petition on 10.08.2022 and only after receiving the notice of the same, the FIR has been lodged by way of counter-blast.

It is further submitted that on account of activities of respondent No.2, a public notice was also published in the newspaper thereby severing relations of applicants with Vivek Singh as well as respondent No.2.
In fact, respondent No.2 is interested in illegally taking possession of house which was purchased by applicants No.2 and 3 by registered sale deed dated 11.04.2019.

It is further submitted that the applicants have also made a complaint to SHO, Police Station Bahodapur,
District Gwalior alleging that respondent No.2 and her brother are illegally residing in the house.
It is further submitted that applicants No.2 and 3 are residing separately which is evident from voter I.D. of Bhaunpura and Kishanpura.
It is further submitted that it is clear from the Samagra I.D. of applicant No.1 that he is residing in Bhonpura, Janpad Panchayat Ambah, District Morena.
Applicant No.2 is working in a private company at Bharuch which is evident from his salary slip.
Thus, it is submitted that the applicants have been falsely implicated.
It is also submitted that allegations of unnatural sex is false but it is fairly conceded that no such allegation was made against the present applicants.

5 . Per contra , counsel for the State by referring to the arrest memos of applicants No.2 and 3 submitted that they are residents of of Sagartal Square, District Gwalior whereas applicant No.1 is the resident of Kishanpura, Ambah, District Morena.

It is submitted that even if applicant No.1 is residing separately NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19772 5 MCRC-6925-2024 in Kishanpura, Ambah, District Morena still in view of the specific allegation that he along with applicant No.2 had taken Rs.10,00,000/- from parents of respondent No.2 in the name of loan and have not returned the same and respondent No.2 was abused and maltreated whenever demand for refund of said amount was made, it is submitted that a prima facie case has been made out against applicant No.1 also.
So far as applicants No.2, 3 and 4 are concerned, it is submitted that there are specific allegations against them which do not warrant quashment of FIR or criminal proceedings.

6. None for respondent No.2 though served.

sentences.text: For example, we may take up one of the findings of the High Court as noted hereinabove.
The High Court has drawn an adverse inference on account of the FIR being lodged on 31-12-2001 while the appellant was forced out of the matrimonial home on 25-5- 2001.

15. In our view, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the High Court was not justified in drawing an adverse inference against the appellant wife for lodging the FIR on 31-12- 2001 on the ground that she had left the matrimonial home at least six months before that.

This is because, in our view, the High Court had failed to appreciate that the appellant and her family members were, during this period,
making all possible efforts to enter into a settlement so that Respondent 2 husband would take her back to the matrimonial home.

If any complaint was made during this period, there was every possibility of not entering into NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19772 6 MCRC-6925-2024 any settlement with Respondent 2 husband.

16. It is pertinent to note that the complaint was filed only when all efforts to return to the matrimonial home had failed and Respondent 2 husband had filed a divorce petition under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

That apart, in our view, filing of a divorce petition in a civil court cannot be a ground to quash criminal proceedings under Section 482 of the Code as it is well settled that criminal and civil proceedings are separate and independent and the pendency of a civil proceeding cannot bring to an end a criminal proceeding even if they arise out of the same set of facts.

Such being the position, we are, therefore, of the view that the High Court while exercising its powers under Section 482 of the Code has gone beyond the allegations made in the FIR and has acted in excess of its jurisdiction and, therefore, the High Court was not justified in quashing the FIR by going beyond the allegations made in the FIR or by relying on extraneous considerations.

22. For the reasons aforesaid, we are inclined to interfere with the order of the High Court and hold that the High Court in quashing the FIR in the exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code by relying on the investigation report and the findings made therein has acted beyond its jurisdiction.

For the purpose of finding out the commission of a cognizable offence, the High Court was only required to look into the allegations made in the complaint or the FIR and to conclude whether a prima facie offence had been made out by the complainant in the FIR or the complaint or not."
9. Therefore, it is clear that merely because FIR has been lodged after filing of divorce petition, the same cannot be quashed on the ground that it was lodged by way of counterblast.
The findings recorded by Civil Court are not binding on the criminal court and criminal case has to proceed on the basis of the allegations made therein.
The degree of proof in civil case and criminal case are different.

If the FIR is lodged after filing of divorce petition then it can also be said that the wife was interested in saving her matrimonial house, therefore, she kept quiet and only when she realized that now the things have crossed all the limits and there is no possibility of reconciliation and decides to make a complaint with regard to atrocities committed by her in-laws
, then it cannot be said that the FIR was lodged by way of counterblast.

sentences.text: In the present case, the complaint is as follows: "Sir, it is submitted that I was married on 18-11- 2009 with Sidharath Parakh s/o Manak Chand Parakh r/o Sarafa Bazar in front of Radha Krishna Market, Gwalior according to the Hindu rites and customs.
In the marriage my father had given gold and silver ornaments, cash amount and household goods according to his capacity.
After the marriage when I went to my matrimonial home, I was treated nicely by the members of the family.

When on the second occasion I went to my matrimonial home, my husband,
father-in-law and mother-in-law started harassing me for not bringing the dowry and started saying that I should bring from my father 25-30 tolas of gold and Rs 2,00,000 in cash and only then they would keep me in the house otherwise not.
On account of this my husband also used to beat me and my father-in-law and my mother-in-law used to torture me by giving the taunts.
In this connection I used to tell my father Kundanmal Oswal, my mother Smt Prem Lata Oswal, uncle Ashok Rai Sharma and uncle Ved Prakash Mishra from time to time.
On 2- 4-2010 the members of the family of my matrimonial home forcibly sent me to the house of my parents in Ganj Basoda along with my brother Deepak.
They snatched my clothes and ornaments and kept with them.
Since then till today my husband has been harassing me on the telephone and has not come to take me back.
Being compelled, I have been moving this application before you.

Sir, it is prayed that action be taken against husband Sidharath Parakh, my father-in-law Manak Chand Parakh and my mother-in-law Smt Indira Parakh for torturing me on account of demanding dowry."

12. There are specific allegations against applicant No.1 that he along with applicant no.2 took Rs.10,00,000/- from the parents of respondent No.2 in the name of loan and whenever the same was demand back then respondent No.2 was harassed and treated with cruelty.
So far applicants No.2, 3 and 4 are concerned there are specific allegations with regard to maltreatment and harassment on account of demand of dowry.
Furthermore, respondent No.2 was ousted from her matrimonial house.

The Supreme Court in the case of Rupali Devi Vs. State of U.P. reported in (2019) 5 SCC 384 has held that mental cruelty may persist even after the wife has left the matrimonial house and has held as under:
"14. "Cruelty" which is the crux of the offence under Section 498-A IPC is defined in Black's Law Dictionary to mean "the intentional and malicious infliction of mental or physical suffering on a living creature, esp. a human; abusive treatment; outrage (abuse, inhuman treatment, indignity)".

sentences.text: Cruelty can be both physical or mental cruelty.

The impact on the mental health of the wife by overt acts on the part of the husband or his relatives; the mental stress and trauma of being driven away from the matrimonial home and her helplessness to go back to the same home for fear of being ill-treated are aspects that cannot be ignored while understanding the meaning of the expression "cruelty" appearing in Section 498- A of the Penal Code.

The emotional distress or psychological effect on the wife, if not the physical injury, is bound to continue to traumatise the wife even after she leaves the matrimonial home and takes shelter at the parental home.

Even if the acts of physical cruelty committed in the matrimonial house may have ceased and such acts do not occur at the parental home,
there can be no doubt that the mental trauma and the psychological distress caused by the acts of the husband including verbal exchanges, if any, that had compelled the wife to leave the matrimonial home and take shelter with her parents would continue to persist at the parental home.

Mental cruelty borne out of physical cruelty or abusive and humiliating verbal exchanges would continue in the parental home even though there may not be any overt act of physical cruelty at such place."

13. Similarly, this Court in the case of in the case of Amar Singh vs. Smt. NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19772 9 MCRC-6925-2024 Vimla decided on 22.06.2021 in Criminal Revision No.2376/2020 (Gwalior Bench) has held that compelling a married women to live in her parental home amounts to cruelty.

That apart, in our view, filing of a divorce petition in a civil court cannot be a ground to quash criminal proceedings under Section 482 of the Code as it is well settled that criminal and civil proceedings are separate and independent and the pendency of a civil proceeding cannot bring to an end a criminal proceeding even if they arise out of the same set of facts.
Such being the position, we are, therefore, of the view that the High Court while exercising its powers under Section 482 of the Code has gone beyond the allegations made in the FIR and has acted in excess of its jurisdiction and, therefore, the High Court was not justified in quashing the FIR by going beyond the allegations made in the FIR or by relying on extraneous considerations.
22. For the reasons aforesaid, we are inclined to interfere with the order of the High Court and hold that the High Court in quashing the FIR in the exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code by relying on the investigation report and the findings made therein has acted beyond its jurisdiction.
9. Therefore, it is clear that merely because FIR has been lodged after filing of divorce petition, the same cannot be quashed on the ground that it was lodged by way of counterblast.
The findings recorded by Civil Court are not binding on the criminal court and criminal case has to proceed on the basis of the allegations made therein.
The degree of proof in civil case and criminal case are different.
If the FIR is lodged after filing of divorce petition then it can also be said that the wife was interested in saving her matrimonial house, therefore, she kept quiet and only when she realized that now the things have crossed all the limits and there is no possibility of reconciliation and decides to make a complaint with regard to atrocities committed by her in-laws
, then it cannot be said that the FIR was lodged by way of counterblast.
Thus, it is clear that the attempt of respondent No.2 was to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19772 7 MCRC-6925-2024 protect her matrimonial life and if she did not lodge the FIR at the earliest, then it cannot be said to be a counterblast.
The Supreme Court in the cases of Kans Raj v. State of Punjab, reported in (2000)
5 SCC 207, Monju Roy v. State of W.B., (2015) 13 SCC 693, Chandralekha & Ors. v. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2013 (1) UC 155, Geeta Mehrotra Vs. State of U.P. reported in (2012)
10 SCC 741,
Even otherwise in the light of judgments passed by the Supreme Court in the cases of XYZ v.
State of Gujarat reported in (2019) 10 SCC 337, State of Tamil Nadu Vs. S. Martin & Ors. reported in (2018) 5 SCC 718, Ajay Kumar Das v. State of Jharkhand, reported in (2011) 12 SCC 319, Mohd.
Akram Siddiqui v. State of Bihar reported in (2019) 13 SCC 350, State of A.P. v. Gourishetty Mahesh reported in (2010) 11 SCC 226, M. Srikanth v. State of Telangana, reported in (2019) 10 SCC 373,
CBI v. Arvind Khanna reported in (2019) 10 SCC 686, State of MP Vs. Kunwar Singh by order dated 30.06.2021 passed in Cr.A. No.709/2021, Munshiram v. State of Rajasthan, reported in (2018) 5 SCC 678, Teeja Devi v. State of Rajasthan reported in (2014) 15 SCC 221, State of Orissa v. Ujjal Kumar Burdhan, reported in (2012) 4 SCC 547, S. Khushboo v. Kanniammal reported in (2010) 5 SCC 600, Sangeeta Agrawal v. State of U.P., NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19772 10 MCRC-6925-2024 reported in (2019) 2 SCC 336, Amit Kapoor v. Ramesh Chander reported in (2012) 9 SCC 460, Padal Venkata Rama Reddy Vs. Kovuri Satyanarayana Reddy reported in (2012)
12 SCC 437 and M.N. Ojha v. Alok Kumar Srivastav reported in (2009) 9 SCC 682 , this Court can quash the proceedings only if the uncontroverted allegations do not make out an offence.
From the plain reading of FIR, it cannot be said that the allegations do not make out a cognizable offence.
